Daily Digest · Computer Science

Video and 3D Models Learn Physical Grounding

Today's submissions reveal a maturing landscape where generative models are being retrofitted with spatial reasoning, physical consistency checks, and embodied understanding. From camera control in video diffusion to sensorimotor alignment in robotics, researchers are moving beyond plausibility toward verifiable physical coherence. A parallel thread tackles efficiency: lightweight interventions (motion gates, selective preprocessing, sparse representations) are replacing brute-force computation.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Computer Vision
PhysTrace pinpoints temporal violations in video models

Video generative models are increasingly trusted for world modeling, yet their physical consistency has been opaque. PhysTrace uses MLLMs to identify which history-conditioned expectations actually conflict with observed dynamics, enabling interpretable temporal localization of physics failures without task-specific probes.

First framework to temporally localize and describe physical violations in pretrained video models without retraining.
Yoo, Jung et al. 2610.31429 PDF
Computer Vision
Gate3DGen selectively cleanses real-world image inputs

Single-image 3D generation fails dramatically on real photos with blur, occlusion, and uneven lighting—but knowing when to intervene matters. Gate3DGen gates preprocessing decisions per-image, preserving clean inputs unchanged while purifying degraded ones, all without retraining downstream 3D generators.

Degradation-aware routing achieves selective purification that preserves visual cues needed for faithful 3D geometry.
Li, Huang et al. 2610.31649 PDF
AI Safety
RIDAR detects and intervenes on research integrity violations

Autonomous research agents can unknowingly violate reproducibility and faithfulness standards. RIDAR introduces RIVT, a taxonomy of 14 research integrity violation types spanning the full lifecycle, and detects them in agent trajectories with 85.2% F1, enabling runtime intervention before harm.

Comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types with detection framework achieving 85.2% F1 on agent trajectory auditing.
Siow, Xin et al. 2610.31372 PDF
Robotics
Sensorimotor alignment predicts embodied policy success offline

Evaluating robotic foundation models typically requires expensive closed-loop rollouts. Sensorimotor Alignment (S²) proposes that motion trajectories form a third modality toward which vision and language representations converge—enabling cheap offline proxies for embodied capability without simulation.

Motion trajectory structure serves as training-free proxy for robotic model capability, eliminating costly evaluation loops.
Xie, Qian et al. 2610.31670 PDF

WorldForge V2: Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion

Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors but struggle with precise camera control and spatial-temporal consistency. WorldForge V2 achieves accurate camera control while preserving pretrained generative capabilities, avoiding visual artifacts and computational overhead of existing task-specific approaches.

02
Gate3DGen: Selective Purification for Real-World 3D Generation

Single-image 3D generation degrades sharply on real-world images with lighting, blur, and occlusions. Gate3DGen introduces a degradation-aware router that selectively preprocesses problematic inputs while leaving clean images unchanged, without retraining downstream generators.

03
PYTHIA: Transferable ML for Material Defect and Site Optimization

Machine learning for material optimization typically requires extensive sampling, limiting applicability to understudied materials. PYTHIA combines foundational models and transfer learning to extend ML applicability to novel material families with minimal data.

cs.LGKouroudis, Gu, GagliardiPDF
04
LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality

Existing local anomaly detection methods excel on industrial benchmarks but fail when inlier distributions are multimodal. LACToS proposes a principled approach using superpixel-level typicality that generalizes across contexts and inlier complexity.

cs.CVcs.LGHong, Kheirandish, Fridovich-KeilPDF
05
Sparse Topometric Graphs for Cross-Session Indoor Navigation

Indoor navigation agents typically accumulate noisy sensor measurements and heavy inference. This work proposes sparse topometric graphs capturing room connectivity and navigable passages, providing training-free structural guidance that complements local observations.

PhysTrace: Interpretable Temporal Evaluation of Physical Consistency

World models assume pretrained video models capture physical dynamics, yet existing evaluations rarely identify which physical expectations conflict with observations. PhysTrace uses MLLM-generated expectations to temporally localize violations and provide interpretable descriptions.

07
Efficient LLM Adaptation for Low-Resource Bashkir Language

Bashkir is a low-resource agglutinative language underrepresented in modern LLMs. This work presents the Bashkir Web Corpus (46.9M tokens) and benchmarks adaptation methods across eight architectures using full fine-tuning, QLoRA, and in-context learning.

08
Task-Centric Survey of Long-Document Visual Question Answering

Visual document understanding increasingly matters for knowledge extraction from visually rich documents. This task-centric survey decomposes long-document VQA into parsing, evidence retrieval, generation, and evaluation, emphasizing how task bottlenecks drive technical choices.

09
RIDAR: Safeguarding Autonomous Research Agents via Detection

Autonomous research agents automate large portions of scientific work but are prone to research integrity violations compromising validity and reproducibility. RIDAR introduces RIVT taxonomy of 14 violation types and achieves 85.2% F1 on post-hoc RIV detection.

cs.AISiow, Xin, WangPDF
10
HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction

Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models work well on short windows but cannot scale to thousands of frames due to memory constraints. HiP3R uses hierarchical pose graph optimization to achieve global consistency by propagating constraints across adjacent overlaps and distant revisits.

11
Evaluating Open LLMs on Spanish MIR Medical Examination

Medical exam accuracy is standard evidence for LLM clinical utility, but deployments need finer signals: uncertainty awareness, sound reasoning, and actual image use. This work evaluates four open models (8-27B parameters) on 1,552 questions across eight Spanish MIR editions.

Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering LLM Representations

Metaphor is central to human cognition, yet its representation in LLMs remains opaque. Using mechanistic interpretability, this work identifies causal subspaces for metaphor in multiple architectures and demonstrates steering on both classification and generation tasks.

Training Small LMs for Transferable Tool Selection

LLM agents operating over thousands of tools face a bottleneck in selecting the right one for multi-step instructions. This work trains small open models via RL to match proprietary LLM decomposition performance on ToolBench, achieving comparable tool selection functionality.

LLM Inference Optimizations on Apple Silicon Applicability

Nearly all LLM inference optimizations target server GPUs, yet Apple Silicon is widely used for local inference. This work evaluates KV-cache pruning, speculative decoding, ported kernels, and quantization across four Apple machines to determine which optimizations retain benefits.

MoG-VLM: Motion-Guided Video Anomaly Detection Framework

Vision-Language Models excel at video anomaly detection but dense frame inference is impractical for real-time deployment. MoG-VLM uses Temporal Gradient Magnitude as a lightweight signal to trigger VLM inference only when motion indicates relevant content, enabling efficient acceleration.

MixPT: Point Transformer with Interleaved Attention Patterns

Point cloud transformers balance computational cost against capturing local geometry and scene-wide relationships. MixPT interleaves window and global attention to efficiently enable scene-wide token interaction without prohibitive scaling.

DIAL: Steerable Language Models via Distilled Adherence Levels

Users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence (e.g., response length), but prompting alone cannot reliably provide fine-grained control. DIAL enables steerable LLMs with numerical control over instruction-following degree across diverse instructions.

Rate-Controlled KV Re-selection for Multimodal Generation

KV cache compression for multimodal LLMs typically selects visual tokens once at prefill, but long-form generation requires evidence that moves as output unfolds. This work proposes drift-triggered re-selection with budget control, achieving superior ROUGE-L on extended descriptions.

19
SyRA-CS: Synthetic-to-Real Adaptation for Code-Switched ASR

Code-switched automatic speech recognition is difficult because real data is scarce and synthetic mismatches reality. SyRA-CS uses Reptile meta-learning to train on synthetic code-switched speech, then adapt with one hour of labeled real speech, evaluated on four architectures.

MVLoMa: Multi-View Local Feature Matching Framework

Local feature matching is typically formulated for image pairs, but structure-from-motion and localization involve matching one reference against many neighbors. MVLoMa extends pairwise matching to sparse star graphs, exploiting complementary multi-view geometric evidence while reducing computation.

Practical Auditing of Differentially Private Graph Release Mechanisms

Differential privacy protects graph data releases, yet empirical auditing has largely targeted tabular datasets, not graph-structured outputs. This work presents methodology for auditing DP graph mechanisms, identifies graph-specific design problems, and provides open-source toolkit.

Entanglement-Induced Feature Maps in Projected Quantum Kernels

Projected quantum kernels circumvent exponential Hilbert space hardness but rely heavily on classical hyperparameter tuning. This work explores the structural characteristics of quantum feature maps and their representational power independent of extensive tuning.

EpiSEM-Bench: Safety and Evidence Recovery Under Missing Evidence

Tool-using LLM agents rely on environmental facts for safety decisions, but omitted safety-relevant facts can lead to prohibited actions. EpiSEM-Bench provides 300 unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains to evaluate unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery.

Agentic Auditing of Multilingual Corpus Quality Control

Multilingual pipelines like FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving failure modes unanticipated. This work demonstrates LLM-as-corpus-debugger: an agent explores Slovak FineWeb2 and compiles executable tests validated by native speakers, finding 1.4M machine-generated documents.

Featured Researcher
CL
Chen Change Loy
Researcher · S-Lab, NTU

Chen Change Loy leads research in computer vision with a focus on long-horizon 3D reconstruction, low-level vision, and efficient geometric understanding. His work on HiP3R demonstrates sophisticated handling of long-sequence consistency through hierarchical pose graph optimization, a critical capability for practical vision systems. Featured today for advancing scalable 3D reconstruction from thousands of video frames while maintaining global geometric coherence.
